story.value: Neptunium is named after the planet Neptune, which was named after the Roman god of the sea.
Neptunium was first produced in 1940 by Edwin M. McMillian and Philip H. Abelson at the University of California, Berkeley.
There were many early false reports of the discovery of neptunium, and the most significant one was by Enrico Fermi.

uses.value: A form of neptunium made in nuclear reactors is used in neutron detectors.
